label: SMOKE fixture — Reuters fact check (misleading element)
summary: Reuters reported that the U.S. construction period began in 1904 and about 5,600 people died during it. The earlier French effort had an estimated 20,000 deaths; the U.S. spent $326 million, which was the most expensive U.S. public-works project at that time, but the combined figures do not support the claim that 38,000 died during U.S. construction.
title: Fact Check: Donald Trump's inaugural speech examined
nuance: Misleading or context-lacking element of the claim.
